title: CERT-In issues advisory against AI-driven cyber attacks for MSMEs, organisations and individuals
body:
MC Logo

India’s national cybersecurity agency Indian Computer Emergency Response Team has issued a detailed advisory warning about the growing risks from artificial intelligence-powered cyber attacks. The advisory highlights how advances in AI are enabling attackers to automate complex cyber operations, reduce the time needed to exploit vulnerabilities, and scale attacks across systems and users. [...] On patch management, CERT-In has urged organisations to reduce the time taken to apply updates. Critical vulnerabilities should be patched within 24 hours, particularly for internet-facing systems. The agency also recommends automating patching processes, maintaining an inventory of IT assets, and prioritising fixes based on exposure and exploit likelihood. [...] In terms of cyber hygiene, CERT-In recommends enforcing strong password policies, disabling unused services, maintaining secure offline backups, and deploying updated endpoint protection tools. Encryption of data at rest and in transit, along with controlled outbound network access, is also advised.
